name: Decade Numerative

dimensions.function: Base for compound formation; determiner, factor
dimensions.distribution: Combines with single-digits to form compounds (twenty-one)

projection.target: Sixty can stand by itself and can supply the first component of sixty-four. The relation to six is transparent, but a new decade form cannot automatically be generated from any numerical expression by adding -ty.
projection.evidence: CGEL treats the decade endings as lexical word formation. Reynolds uses decade-based compounds as evidence for the basic lexicon.

curious.title: Number words for whole tens
curious.summary: The words twenty to ninety each name a number of tens.
curious.body:
Twenty means 20, and seventy means 70. These words name whole tens, from twenty up to ninety, and each is built from a single-digit base with the ending -ty.

Sixty stands by itself as a word, and it also supplies the first part of sixty-four. Its link to six is easy to see. But you can't make a new tens word by adding -ty to just any number expression.
curious.try: Say all the tens words from twenty to ninety. Which one reminds you of its single-digit number?

teacher.summary: Covers the tens words twenty to ninety, built with -ty, as the base for numbers like sixty-four.
teacher.explain: A decade numerative specifies a cardinality in tens (20, 30, ..., 90), formed from a single-digit base and the suffix -ty. It's a basic numerative, so it can serve as determiner or factor, and it combines with single digits to form compounds such as twenty-one. Sixty can stand alone and can supply the first component of sixty-four. The relation to six is transparent, but a new decade form can't automatically be generated from any numerical expression by adding -ty. The dictionary treats the decade endings as lexical word formation, and marks this account as provisional.
teacher.terms: Numerative is this grammar's term for number words, where a textbook may say numeral. Decade numerals or tens words are common informal names.
watch_for: A learner might think any number word can take -ty to make a tens word.
A learner might miss that sixty relates to six, though the link is transparent.
teacher.activity: Students write the tens words from twenty to ninety, circle each ending, and match each with its single-digit base. Then they build three compound numbers from them.

child.hook: What do twenty, thirty and forty all end with?
child.explain: Words like twenty, seventy and ninety name whole tens. They end in -ty. Seventy means 70. You can count by tens with them.
child.play: Count by tens out loud, from twenty up to ninety. Stop at each -ty word, and clap on each one.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Decade Numerative." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/numerative-decade-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
